newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end strong, H shares leap ahead.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end strong, H shares leap ahead.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks advanced to a strong finish on Tuesday, bolstered by bullish local and overseas sentiment, brokers said.
"We're still in a bull market," said Julian Ings-Chambers, sales director at BZW Securities.

The Hang Seng Index closed 198.23 points up at 13,342.46, off the day's high of 13,360.45. Trading activity remained robust with turnover reaching HK$9.16 billion, higher than Monday's HK$8.54 billion.
"We're seeing a lot of loose money come back into the market from (unsuccessful) new issue subscriptions," said Ings-Chambers.

Oversubscriptions of new issues by Guangdong Tannery and Hong Kong Solartech were examples of the keen desire by local investors to get into the market as well as the amount of loose money available, he said.

Solartech's offer of 125 million shares at HK$1.20 a share was 121 times oversubscribed, tying up nearly HK$19 billion. Guangdong Tannery's small public offer of 30 million shares at HK$1.03 a share was 667 oversubscribed, sweeping up more than HK$20 billion.
But brokers said a good portion of the afternoon trading activity was from European institutions.
"Institutions are taking a cautious but bullish approach now," said Patrick Ho, dealer at UBS Securities.
Buying in H shares was a key feature of the market on Tuesday, brokers said.

"The liberalisation of currency controls in China has spurred the rise in the Shanghai and Shenzhen markets and the interest in H shares derives from that trend," said a broker with a large European house.
The Hang Seng China Enterprise Index jumped 9.97 percent to 929.55 compared with the 1.51 percent rise in the blue-chip Hang Seng Index.
Leading the sector was Zhenhai Refining with a gain of HK$0.50 or 22.47 percent to HK$2.725, followed by Shanghai Haixing Ship with a rise of HK$0.14 or 20.29 percent to HK$0.83.
The commercial and industrial sector led the market, followed by finance. Property shares rebounded from negative territory in the morning to just outperform the market.
Hang Seng Bank was the largest net gainer, putting on HK$2.25 to HK$92.50.
Red chip China Resources was one of the most active issues, rising HK$0.80 to HK$14.80 on heavy volume of HK$278.65 million.
